title: Understanding SVD Components
text: When performing Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), the matrix $X$ is decomposed into three matrices: $U$, $S$, and $V**T$. Consider what each of these matrices represents in terms of dimensions and properties. What can you infer about the structure of $S$ and $V**T$?

hintAnswer: $U$ is $n \times n$, $S$ is $n \times d$, and $V**T$ is $d \times $$d\$$$
title: Matrix Dimensions in SVD
text: Given that $X$ has $n$ rows and $d$ columns, what are the dimensions of the matrices $U$, $S$, and $V**T$ in the decomposition $X=USV**T$?
choices: $U$ is $n \times n$, $S$ is $n \times d$, and $V**T$ is $d \times $$d\$$$
$U$ is $n \times d$, $S$ is $d \times d$, and $V**T$ is $d \times $$n\$$$
$U$ is $d \times n$, $S$ is $d \times d$, and $V**T$ is $n \times $$d\$$$

title: Diagonal Matrix Properties
text: A diagonal matrix has non-zero elements only on its main diagonal. Consider the rank of $X$ and how it affects the structure of $S$. What does this imply about $S$ being a diagonal matrix?

hintAnswer: There are fewer than $d$ $$non-zero$$ singular values in $S$.
title: Rank and Diagonal Matrices
text: If $rank(X)<d$, what does this tell you about the number of non-zero singular values in $S$?
choices: There are fewer than $d$ $$non-zero$$ singular values in $S$.
There are exactly $d$ $$non-zero$$ singular values in $S$.
There are more than $d$ $$non-zero$$ singular values in $S$.
